newsitem.title: UK: British output prices rise 0.2 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: British output prices rise 0.2 pct in January.

text.p: British output prices rose 0.2 percent in January for a 1.5 percent year-on-year rise, official figures showed on Monday.
The figures were better than analysts had expected and appeared to reduce the need for a rise in interest rates, currently 6.0 percent, before an election due by May 22.
The statistics office said the 1.5 percent year-on-year rise was the lowest rate of increase since October 1986.

The Bank of England wants an increase in interest rates to douse down inflationary pressures in the economy but Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke has resisted any move because he does not believe the economy is overheating.
"I'm sure Kenneth Clarke is singing in his bath on these numbers, very good indeed. Across the board these are very impressive figures," said John Shepperd of Yamaichi International.
